name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Use a 2px solid #005fcc focus ring with a 1px white stroke at 75% opacity. This keeps the ring visible against dark backgrounds while staying subtle enough not to distract. The thinner line balances visibility with minimal visual clutter, which matters for users who rely on focus indicators to navigate. Trade-off: it’s slightly less bold than a 3px ring, but that’s acceptable since the 1px white stroke already boosts contrast.

name: Reader
text: The 2px ring still risks failing WCAG 2.2 AA on *very* light backgrounds where the white stroke loses contrast against the background. A 3px ring with a 1px white stroke at 50% opacity would hold contrast better across all backgrounds while keeping the indicator clear for keyboard users. Test with a 1:3 contrast ratio checker on both dark and light modes to settle it.

name: Ramp
text:
Use a 3px solid #005fcc focus ring with a 1px white stroke at 50% opacity. This guarantees WCAG 2.2 AA contrast on *all* backgrounds while keeping the indicator unmistakable for keyboard users. The trade-off is a slightly thicker ring, but clarity for users who need it outweighs minimal extra space.

name: Reader
text: The 3px ring risks feeling heavy on dense interfaces where space is tight. A 2.5px ring with a 0.75px white stroke at 60% opacity would split the difference—still passing WCAG 2.2 AA on light backgrounds without bulk. Test the contrast ratio of both options against #ffffff and #f5f5f5; whichever meets 4.5:1 at both points wins.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Adopt the 2.5px solid #005fcc focus ring with a 0.75px white stroke at 60% opacity. Result: a focus ring that passes WCAG 2.2 AA on #ffffff and #f5f5f5, stays subtle on dense screens, and ships in EXCAVA’s CSS. Owner: Ramp.
